summary: Port draws the same metaball geometry on the same logical canvas, but its simulation evolves ~16-25x too slowly (looks frozen at any normal viewing timescale) and its fire ramp is ~2-4x too bright with no dim half and a rim that clips to R=255.
observations: Control surface MATCHES exactly: both sides expose sliderNumberOfPoints (slider, label NumberOfPoints) and sliderSpeed (slider, label Speed). No compile or runtime errors on either side; both are wantsSensors:false.

MOTION is the headline divergence. Default rig (grid 16x16), untouched dials, 20 fps: orig statsSummary motion avg 2.1 / motionLit avg 9.8 with zeroMotionFrames 1/120; port motion avg 0.1 / motionLit avg 0.5 with zeroMotionFrames 113/120. The port's 12-frame filmstrip (baseline/port-motion.png, 3.00-3.55 s) is visually indistinguishable frame to frame while the original's (baseline/orig-motion.png) redraws completely over the same 0.55 s.

Quantified slowdown factor ~16x untouched. Spatial autocorrelation of the frame between times (121 dumped frames, 0.25 s apart, 30 s window, 20 fps): orig corr(0.25s)=0.62, corr(0.5s)=0.34, corr(1s)=0.09 — fully decorrelated by ~1 s. Port corr(0.5s)=0.93, corr(2s)=0.74, corr(4s)=0.56, corr(8s)=0.34, corr(16s)=0.06. Port needs 8 s to reach the correlation the original reaches in 0.5 s -> 16x.

Quantified slowdown factor ~25x with dials matched. At sliderSpeed=0.5, sliderNumberOfPoints=0.5 on both sides (label dial-decorr, 121 dumps 1.5 s apart over 120 s): orig is already at corr 0.05 by lag 1.5 s; port crosses corr 0.5 at ~10 s. Same conclusion from motionLit at matched dials: orig 8.5 vs port 0.3 (28x) at speed 0.5; orig 13.9 vs port 0.5 (28x) at speed 1.

Centroid speed on the default rig, untouched, 30 s window: orig brightness-centroid travels 4.94 px/s (148 px of path); port travels 0.64 px/s (19 px). ~7.7x, an underestimate because the orig's centroid also jumps when blobs split.

The port's underlying SIMULATION is right, just slow. Rendering the port over 96 s (label port-timescaled, i.e. ~16x the original's 6 s baseline window) produces a contact sheet whose blob shapes, sizes, merges, splits and grid positions track the original's 6 s baseline sheet closely (orig 0.55 s cell <-> port 8.7 s cell, etc.). So this is a rate bug, not a different field or a different point motion.

COLOR/BRIGHTNESS is the second major divergence. Aggregated over 121 dumped frames: orig max R ever seen = 178, ZERO pixels clipped, and 68% of lit pixels sit below R=96 (R histogram in 32-wide buckets: 32:36.1%, 64:31.9%, 96:16.9%, 128:10.5%, 160:4.6%). Port max R = 255, 15.0% of lit pixels are fully clipped at R=255, and NO lit pixel is below R=128 (128:21.8%, 160:31.6%, 192:15.9%, 224:30.6%). The port has no dim half of the ramp at all.

Mean brightness follows: orig meanBrightness avg 6.5 (min 3, max 15) vs port 27.7 (min 26, max 30) on the 6 s baseline — port is ~4x too bright and, unlike the original, barely varies (orig swings 3-15, port 26-30).

HUE at the hot end is too red. Cross-section through the blob at t=0 (row 7, default rig): orig runs 105/0, 84/27, 142/62, 130/54, 127/52, 127/52, 139/60, 156/72, 155/71, 143/62, 131/54, 118/47, 79/25, 67/6 (R/G); port runs 255/9, 154/29, 202/53, 193/49, 189/47, 188/47, 191/48, 196/50, 192/49, 187/47, 182/44, 170/38, 153/27, 238/14. Orig core G/R = 0.46 (amber); port core G/R = 0.27 (red-orange). At the faint end both agree on hue (G/R ~0.16-0.17) but the port's R there is 153 where the original's is 51 — 3x.

Bucketing G/R by R across all dumped frames: orig G/R RISES with brightness (0.18 at R 32-64 -> 0.48 at R 160-178) — a proper fire ramp from deep red to amber. Port's apparent G/R FALLS (0.18 at R~128 -> 0.04 at R>=224) purely because its brightest pixels are the clipped rim. Blue is exactly 0 on both sides at all times (meanB avg 0).

The thin bright red rim around each blob is present on BOTH sides — it is a real feature of the original, not a port invention — but the original's rim is R~88-105 with G 0-6 while the port's rim saturates at R=255. The lit fraction is comparable (orig 22.4%, port 26.8% of the 256 px), and the blob EXTENT matches: at t=0 row 7 both sides light x=1..14, so the field/threshold geometry is correct.

Both sides are FRAME-STEPPED, consistently. Rendering the same window at 10/20/40 fps: orig corr(0.5 s) = 0.557 / 0.342 / 0.074; port corr(0.5 s) = 0.977 / 0.927 / 0.853. Speed scales with fps on both, so there is no frame-rate-coupling MISMATCH — the port is simply taking a step ~16x too small per frame. Confirmed independently: the original's zigzag in the rhythm image has a constant ~60-frame period at both 2 fps (480 frames / ~8 cycles over 240 s) and 5 fps (300 frames / ~5 cycles over 60 s).

No distinct regimes or modes on either side. 60 s @5 fps and 240 s @2 fps surveys both show a continuous metaball simulation: orig-rhythm.png is a dense zigzag mesh (blobs sweeping across and bouncing back); port-rhythm.png is near-vertical columns with only a slow drift, over the whole 240 s.

Global brightness cycle: autocorrelation of meanBrightness over a 6000-frame run (300 s @20 fps, untouched) gives the original a fundamental at 287 frames (14.3 s) with a sub-peak at 46 f; the port's earliest strong peak is 806 frames with clean harmonics at 1572 and 2324 f — ~2.8x longer. This factor did not reproduce cleanly across dial settings, so treat it as secondary to the 16-25x spatial figure.

RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE matches. Re-rendered at --grid 48x48, both sides draw the SAME logical picture as at 16x16, just finer — same blob count, same relative sizes. The 48x48 render also makes the colour gap obvious: the original shows a bright amber/yellow hot core per metaball inside a dark red halo, while the port is a near-uniform red-orange mass with a thin saturated red rim and almost no core contrast.
Contrast within a blob is compressed on the port: orig row-7 interior spans R 84-156 (1.86x), port spans R 153-202 (1.32x).
Steady state is fine on both sides — no decay, no freeze-to-black, no saturation drift. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both across 6 s, 12 s, 60 s, 96 s, 240 s and 300 s windows.

Seed-independent character on both sides (seeds 1, 7, 1234): orig meanBrightness 6.5/8.7/8.6 with motionLit 9.8/7.3/7.0; port 27.7/27.5/21.9 with motionLit 0.5/0.5/0.6. The divergence is not a one-seed fluke.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Live and roughly linear in the animation rate. At NumberOfPoints=0.5, 12 s @20 fps: motionLit avg 0 (frozen, zeroMotionFrames 240/240) at 0, then 4.3 at 0.25, 8.5 at 0.5, 11.3 at 0.75, 13.9 at 1. Probe maxDelta 15.68 / maxDeltaLit 36.27.
dials.portEffect: Live and in the SAME DIRECTION, but ~28x too weak at every setting: motionLit avg 0 at 0 (correctly frozen), 0.2 at 0.25, 0.3 at 0.5, 0.4 at 0.75, 0.5 at 1. zeroMotionFrames stays 232-237 out of 240 even at full speed. Probe maxDelta 6.66 / maxDeltaLit 16.35. The port at sliderSpeed=1 is no faster than the original at roughly sliderSpeed=0.03; note also that the port's untouched default already matches its own maximum (motionLit 0.5), so there is no headroom in the dial to compensate.

dials.name: sliderNumberOfPoints
dials.origEffect: Live: more points -> brighter, denser, more overlapping blobs. At Speed=0.5, 12 s @20 fps, meanBrightness avg 6.7 / 8.1 / 11.6 / 12.8 / 12.8 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 (a ~1.9x span). Visually at 0 the sheet shows one main blob plus a couple of small satellites; at 1 it shows a sprawling chain of merged blobs plus several satellites. Probe maxDelta 17.83 / maxDeltaLit 37.26.
dials.portEffect: Live and in the same direction but with a compressed span, and the value is swamped by the over-bright ramp: meanBrightness avg 22.2 / 25.3 / 26.3 / 25.5 / 24.8 at the same settings (a ~1.2x span, and non-monotonic above 0.5). Blob count/shape at 0 vs 1 does track the original qualitatively (one blob vs one large irregular blob with satellites), but because the port barely moves, the difference is much harder to see. Probe maxDelta 29.87 / maxDeltaLit 54.49 (inflated by the port's high absolute brightness).

feedback: PRIMARY FIX — animation rate. The port's metaball point positions advance ~16x too little per frame at untouched defaults and ~25-28x too little with sliderSpeed matched at 0.5 or 1. Multiply the per-frame position step by ~16-20x so that the whole-frame spatial autocorrelation drops from 1.0 to ~0.34 in about 0.5 s at 20 fps (currently it takes ~8 s), and so that the brightness-centroid travels ~5 px/s on a 16x16 grid rather than 0.6 px/s. Target statsSummary on a 6 s / 20 fps default-rig run: motion avg ~2, motionLit avg ~10, zeroMotionFrames ~1 of 120 (currently motion 0.1, motionLit 0.5, zeroMotionFrames 113).

The speed dial's RANGE also needs rescaling, not just the default: the original goes from frozen at 0 to motionLit ~13.9 at 1, roughly linearly (4.3 / 8.5 / 11.3 / 13.9 at 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1). The port goes 0 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.5. Both endpoints are wrong — the zero endpoint is correct (both correctly freeze), so the fix is a single gain on the speed term, applied where the dial value is turned into a per-frame step.

Both sides are frame-stepped (speed scales with fps identically on both), so do NOT convert the port to time-based integration while fixing this — that would introduce a mismatch that currently does not exist. Just scale the per-frame step.

SECONDARY FIX — the fire ramp is far too hot at its dim end and clips at its bright end. The original never exceeds R=178 and never clips; 68% of its lit pixels sit below R=96 and 36% below R=64, so most of the picture is deep dim red on black. The port emits NO lit pixel below R=128 and clips 15% of its lit pixels flat at R=255. Rescale the intensity-to-colour mapping so the faintest lit pixel is around R~35-50 (currently ~130-153) and the rim tops out near R~100-105 (currently 255), keeping the blob EXTENT unchanged — the lit-pixel set and the threshold geometry are already correct (both sides light x=1..14 on row 7 at t=0).

SECONDARY FIX — hue at the hot end. The original's core is amber, G/R ~0.46-0.48 at R 160-178; the port's core is red-orange, G/R ~0.27 at R~210. Push more green into the top of the ramp. The dim end already matches (both G/R ~0.16-0.17), so the ramp needs to travel further toward amber, not be shifted wholesale.

After the brightness fix, re-check the NumberOfPoints dial: the original's mean brightness spans ~1.9x from dial 0 to dial 1 (6.7 -> 12.8) while the port spans only ~1.2x (22.2 -> 26.3) and is non-monotonic above 0.5. Some of that compression is just the saturated ramp clipping away the difference, but confirm the point COUNT itself scales the same way once the ramp is corrected.

Within-blob contrast is compressed on the port (row-7 interior spans 1.86x on the original, 1.32x on the port). The original shows a clearly brighter hot core per metaball inside a darker halo — this reads best at --grid 48x48. Once the ramp is rescaled, verify each metaball has a visibly distinct hot core rather than a uniform mass.

Geometry, threshold, rim structure, resolution independence, frame-stepping behaviour, control names/kinds/labels and dial directions are all already correct — do not touch those. This should be fixable with a speed gain and a colour-ramp rescale.
